newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil swaps-mogas tarnished after hefty selloff.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil swaps-mogas tarnished after hefty selloff.

text.p: Gasoline, ever the leader of the energy swaps pack dealt the markets a glancing blow on Thursday as heavy pre-expiry NYMEX selling threatened to stop its rise.
But because most of the sell-off pressure was focused on August NYMEX with further out contracts less affected dealers said the fall from grace of gasoline was premature.
Gasoline swaps ended the day 50 cents or so stronger than Wednesday and some $1-2 off the highs talked before the NYMEX sell-off.
Brent crude CFDs were firmer by a few cents with while naphtha held steady and fuel was flat.
"It was gasoline's day, the others have had to take a back seat," said one trader.
August gasoline stretched to reach $207-208 before being pulled down to $205-206 towards the end of the day. September's backwardation held at around $9 with October lower again by $5 or so.
Naphtha piggy-backed on gasoline taking the knocks with the gains and finished the day essentially even against Wednesday. August was put at $191.50-192.00 with September backwardated by $4 or so.
Fuel was flat and fairly quiet with August heavy fuel around $91 with September $1 in contango.
Brent CFDs were a few cents firmer with August 4-8 around 10 cents against September Brent from +3 cents amid talk that +10 traded.
August 11-15 was pegged at -2 cents from -4 cents while August 18=22 firmed to -6/7 cents from -10 cents.
